firstQuery: How does AI tutoring compare to traditional instruction?

messages.content: How does AI tutoring compare to traditional instruction?

The corpus suggests that **AI tutoring generally outperforms or adds value beyond traditional instruction**, but the strength of evidence varies by context. In K-12 math, a meta-analysis of **18 studies and 77 effect sizes** found that intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) had a **statistically significant positive effect** on U.S. students’ learning outcomes, with a pooled effect of **g = 0.271** [Do intelligent tutoring systems benefit K-12 students? 2025]. A separate review of K-12 AI-driven ITS reported that **Cognitive Tutor Algebra I** improved algebra proficiency after sustained use, with effects becoming more visible in the **second year** and especially in **high schools**; middle-school effects were similar in direction but not significant (**+0.20 SD**) [A systematic review of AI-driven intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) in K-12 education 2025].

Individual studies also show that AI tutoring can beat a non-AI version of the **same system** or improve results when paired with human instruction. In a randomized trial with **78 middle school students (grades 6–8)**, an ITS with **automated real-time feedback** led to larger gains in math performance than the same ITS without feedback; scores rose from **1.90 to 3.54** in the feedback group versus **1.90 to 2.85** in the no-feedback group, with a significant interaction (**F=9.240, p=.003, partial η²=.108**) [Enhancing Students’ Learning Outcomes in Mathematics through Intelligent Tutoring Systems Based on Real-Time Feedback 2025]. In a much larger live K-12 tutoring trial, **4,136 tutoring sessions** showed that tutors using **Tutor CoPilot** were **4 percentage points more likely** to get students to pass the session exit ticket (**62% to 66%**, **0.040**) [Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise 2025]. That suggests AI can also enhance **human-led tutoring**, not just stand alone.

At the same time, the corpus does **not** support claiming AI tutoring is universally better than traditional instruction in every setting. A STEM review found broad positive learning effects across **22 studies**, but outcomes ranged from **no detectable impact to as high as 1.24**, and it explicitly notes **no evidence that these gains match expert human tutors** [A Systematic Review of Literature on the Effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems in STEM 2021]. More recent reviews also describe the evidence as **mixed** in real-world settings, even while highlighting benefits from personalization and adaptive support [A Comprehensive Review of AI-based Intelligent Tutoring Systems 2025]. So the best corpus-based summary is: **AI tutoring usually beats business-as-usual or weaker comparison conditions, especially in math/STEM, but it has not yet been shown to consistently surpass expert human tutoring across contexts**
